chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Sid Catlett at the Downbeat
summary: On a break he hears Sid Catlett with Allan Eager's quartet.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In fact, that's where I first heard the great Sid Catlett. While we were playing at the Club Alabam, we were playing for the big production and we were doing our thing. Melvin White... We also had another fine singer named Estelle Edmonson(?) with the band. And on my break, I walked down to the Downbeat, and Sid Catlett was playing the drums in the Downbeat. They had a very fine tenor player with them. His name was Allan Eager. He eventually went into race-car driving and a whole lot of other things. But they had a great quartet in there.

And I never will forget, when I entered the door, I could feel the pulsation from those drums, Sid Catlett... And it was something. Like, the beat met you at the door! And it was not loud. It was just plush. He was a big man with finesse, you know. He had plenty of finesse, and was very high on his instrument, you know. In fact, when what they call the Bebop Movement first started, he was one of the few drummers that could adapt to it, that had the equipment and the willingness to adapt to the thing. He
made some of the early records, you know. And that was a real treat, to hear him play.
